title: Unobstructed deformations of a separated curve with isolated lci singularities
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A scheme over a field is a local complete intersection if it has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated local-complete-intersection algebras [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Assume $X$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ and is smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] except at finitely many points. A local ring here is a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal; an Artinian ring is one whose ideals satisfy the descending chain condition. For a Noetherian local ring $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with specified residue field $k$, let $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$ be the category of Artinian local $\Lambda$-algebras $A$ with a specified identification $A/\mathfrak m_A\cong k$, and local $\Lambda$-homomorphisms inducing the identity on $k$. A deformation of a $k$-scheme $X$ over $A$ is a flat scheme $X_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with an identification $X_A\times_A k\cong X$; arrows are isomorphisms compatible with these identifications. The deformation category $\operatorname{Def}_{X,\Lambda}$ is unobstructed if, for every surjection $A^\prime\twoheadrightarrow A$ in $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$ and every deformation $X_A$, there is a flat deformation $X_{A^\prime}$ and an isomorphism $X_{A^\prime}\times_{A^\prime}A\cong X_A$ compatible with the identified special fibres. Then $\operatorname{Def}_{X,\Lambda}$ is unobstructed for every such $\Lambda$. The empty scheme and disconnected schemes are allowed; $X$ need not be proper. Flatness and base change in the deformation definition use [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0DZQ (lemma-curve-isolated-lci), with example-schemes and section-general specifying the coefficient category; here restricted to Noetherian local coefficient rings with residue field exactly k.

proof.text: Let $W$ be the union of the open subschemes of $X$ on which $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. Smoothness is local on the source and remains smooth upon restriction, so $W$ is smooth and its complement $P$ is the nonsmooth locus. By hypothesis $P$ is finite and it is closed by construction. The Jacobson-density statement says that the closed points of $X$ lying in $P$ are dense in $P$. There are finitely many such points, so their union is closed in $X$ and hence in $P$. Density forces this union to equal $P$. Thus every point of $P$ is closed, including when $P$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0DZQ, lemma-curve-isolated-lci, first sentence; finite closed singular set made explicit using varieties.tex Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson).

proof.text: Apply the two-affine-cover statement to $X$ and $P$. It gives $X=U\cup V$ with $P\subset V$, $U\cap P=\varnothing$, affine $U,V,U\cap V$, and smooth $U$ and $U\cap V$ over $k$. All the separatedness, finite-type and dimension hypotheses are those of the item; step 1 supplied the closedness of the points. Apply affine-open locality of the local-complete-intersection property to the assumed affine lci cover of $X$, with the affine open $V$. Hence $V=\operatorname{Spec}P_V$ for a finitely generated local-complete-intersection $k$-algebra $P_V$.

source.place: Tag 0DZQ, proof: choice of U_2 and U_1 (here V and U), and application of lemma-lci-unobstructed to U_2; affine lci locality: morphisms.tex Tag 01UG and algebra.tex Tag 00SH.

proof.text: Fix a coefficient ring $\Lambda$, a surjection $A^\prime\twoheadrightarrow A$ in $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$, and a deformation $Y=X_A$ with special-fibre identification $\iota:Y_k\cong X$. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ is nilpotent. On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Y$, base change to $k$ gives $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak m_AB)$. Every prime of $B$ contains this nilpotent ideal, and the quotient bijection matches $D(b)$ with $D(\bar b)$, so this is a homeomorphism. The chart identifications agree on overlaps, being restrictions of the special-fibre map. Let $Y_V$ correspond to $V$ under $\iota$. For every test scheme $T$, a morphism $T\to Y_k$ factors through $Y_V\times_A k$ exactly when its composite $T\to Y$ lands in $Y_V$: the fibre-product universal property gives the unique factorization. Under $\iota$ this is precisely factorization through $V$. Thus $(Y_V)_k\cong V$ as schemes. Restriction to an open leaves the local-ring maps unchanged, so $Y_V$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0DZQ, last sentence: lemma-affine (Tag 0DYX) and lemma-lci-unobstructed (Tag 0DZH); restriction is lemma-open. The nilpotent-special-fibre chart calculation spells out the restriction.

proof.text: With $P_V$ from step 2 and the flat deformation $Y_V$ from step 3, apply the affine-lci Artinian lifting statement to $A^\prime\twoheadrightarrow A$. Its coefficient rings and specified residue maps are those fixed in step 3, and its lci and finite-generation hypotheses are supplied by step 2. It supplies a flat affine $A^\prime$-scheme $Z$ and an $A$-isomorphism $e:Z\times_{A^\prime}A\cong Y_V$ compatible with the identified special fibre. The statement permits an arbitrary scheme deformation $Y_V$, so no affineness of $Y_V$ is assumed here.

source.place: Tag 0DZQ, last sentence: scheme/algebra equivalence Tag 0DYX (lemma-affine) and affine-lci unobstructedness Tag 0DZH (lemma-lci-unobstructed), applied to V.

proof.text: Use the smooth-open coefficient lifting statement with the cover $X=U\cup V$, the original deformation $Y$, and the prescribed lift $(Z,e)$ of $Y_V$. Step 2 gives precisely its affineness and smoothness hypotheses on $U$ and $U\cap V$; it puts no lci or smoothness condition on $V$ beyond the lift obtained in step 4. The coefficient rings and residue identifications are those fixed in step 3, so this application includes mixed characteristic. We obtain a flat $A^\prime$-scheme $Y^\prime$, an $A$-isomorphism $\alpha:Y^\prime\times_{A^\prime}A\cong Y$, and an $A^\prime$-isomorphism $\gamma:Y^\prime_V\cong Z$ satisfying $e\circ\gamma_A=\alpha|_{Y_V}$. Here the special-fibre identification is $\iota\circ\alpha_k$, and it defines the open $Y^\prime_V$. Thus the global reduction and the chosen affine lift agree over $A$, not merely on the special fibre.

source.place: Tag 0DZQ, penultimate sentence, using Tag 0DZN (lemma-glueing-smooth), second assertion for smooth U_1.

proof.text: Let $\iota:Y_k\cong X$ be the original identification. Give $Y^\prime$ the identification $\iota^\prime=\iota\circ\alpha_k$ of its special fibre with $X$. Thus $\iota\circ\alpha_k=\iota^\prime$ is precisely the compatibility required for $\alpha$ to be an isomorphism of deformations. The chosen identification also restricts to $V$ as used by the gluing statement, since $\alpha$ carries the corresponding opens to one another. The surjection and the deformation were arbitrary, so the stated deformation category is unobstructed. Empty opens give the same argument for the empty scheme.
